conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you've been vomiting and saw something dark in your vomit—can you tell me more about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it looked like coffee grounds. I’ve been vomiting all day. I woke up with high blood sugar and just couldn’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You have type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis, right? That can definitely make nausea worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and I’ve had this before. But the coffee ground part scared me. Is there bleeding?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re concerned about that. Your CT scan showed some changes in the esophagus, possibly from vomiting. We’ll need an endoscopy to check for any tears.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: An endoscopy? Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll be sedated, so you won’t feel it. It’s important to rule out serious bleeding. We also started you on a medication to reduce stomach acid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes me feel better. My stomach pain is gone now, at least.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. We also placed a line in your groin because we couldn’t get an IV in your arm. It’s temporary and will help us give you fluids and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I noticed that. It’s a bit uncomfortable, but I understand why it’s needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep an eye on it. Your labs show your blood sugar was high earlier, but it’s coming down. We’re giving you insulin as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I usually take Lantus at night. Should I still take it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Since you’re not eating, we held your Lantus last night. We’ll restart it gradually. You’re getting Humalog for now based on your sugar levels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I just don’t want my sugar to crash.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re monitoring closely. No signs of low sugar so far. We also saw your potassium was low, so we’re giving supplements.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that before. Is phosphorus low too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, both were low. We’re replacing them through your IV. It should correct over the next day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I’ve been anxious—my heart’s been racing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We noticed your heart rate was high earlier, in the 140s. But when you rested, it came down. It seems related to anxiety, not a heart issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That happens when I’m stressed. Being in the ICU is overwhelming.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll move you to the regular floor soon. It’s quieter and should help you relax.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You just had your endoscopy. The good news is no active bleeding. There’s a small erosion at the junction of your esophagus and stomach, likely from vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the coffee grounds were from that? Not a serious bleed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. It’s called a Mallory-Weiss tear—small and usually heals on its own. We’ll keep you on a strong acid blocker to help it heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Can I start eating soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start with small sips. If you tolerate that, we’ll advance slowly. Your gastroparesis means your stomach empties slowly, so we have to be cautious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ll be patient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are improving. Potassium and phosphorus are normal now. Blood sugar is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. I’ve been sipping broth and haven’t vomited since yesterday afternoon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. We’ll try a soft diet today. We also restarted your metoclopramide to help your stomach empty.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on that before. It helps, but sometimes makes me restless.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll watch for that. If it happens, we can adjust. Your insulin dose is back to normal—20 units Lantus tonight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried about my diabetes being off track again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll need you to monitor sugars closely at home. Same with potassium—your levels dropped this time, so your doctor may check it in a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. Any restrictions when I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Avoid heavy lifting for a few days because of the femoral line site. Otherwise, resume normal activities as tolerated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We removed the femoral line this morning—no issues. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. What meds should I take?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue your usual insulin—Lantus 20 units at night, Humalog with meals. Take metoclopramide with meals, gabapentin twice daily, and Zofran if nausea returns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the lisinopril for blood pressure?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue that daily. Follow up with your primary doctor in a week for labs and to review everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. If you vomit again or see dark stools, come back right away. Otherwise, take care and rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for explaining everything so clearly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. We’re here if you need us. You’re discharged now—someone will help you with the paperwork.
